title: Florida overlay
description: Applies Florida's accessible parking rules from s. 553.5041, F.S. and the Florida Building Code – Accessibility: 12-foot-wide accessible spaces, blue outlines, the state sign wording, and a 44-inch route from the spaces that does not pass behind parked cars.

sources.title: Section 553.5041, Florida Statutes — Parking spaces for persons who have disabilities
Section 101.715, Florida Statutes — Accessibility of polling places for people having a disability
Polling Place Accessibility guide (DE Guide 0014)
sources.publisher: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections

kit.name: Florida “Parking by disabled permit only” sign on a portable stand
kit.description: State-required wording and fine amount, International Symbol of Accessibility.

parking.space-width.help: Florida requires accessible spaces at least 12 feet (144 inches) wide. Measure from the center of one line to the center of the other.

parking.van-combined-width.help: In Florida every accessible space is 12 feet wide with a 5-foot aisle, so a van space and its aisle add up to at least 204 inches.

fix.summary: Create temporary 12-foot accessible spaces closest to the accessible entrance, each with a 5-foot aisle marked by cones and a Florida permit-only sign.

item.prompt: Is each accessible space prominently outlined in blue paint?

fix.summary: Outline the space with blue marking tape for election day and report the faded paint to the facility.

item.prompt: Does each sign read “PARKING BY DISABLED PERMIT ONLY” and show the fine amount?

fix.summary: Place a portable Florida permit-only sign at each space with non-compliant signage.

item.prompt: How wide is the route from the accessible spaces to the entrance, at its narrowest?
item.help: Florida requires a route at least 44 inches wide that does not make voters walk or wheel behind parked cars other than their own.

fix.summary: Cone off a 44-inch path from the accessible spaces to the walkway so voters do not pass behind parked cars.
